dataset.name: Monitoring of ground water table depth and soil moisture at the Point Reyes field site
description: Ground water table (GWT) depth and soil moisture (SM) have been monitored at several locations at the Point Reyes field site (Californian coastal grassland) from 2021 to 2024. Monitoring is still on-going and data may be added to this archive at later time. The SM data have been acquired using Teros 12 Meter soil moisture sensors placed at 10, 30, 60 and 90 cm depth at 5 locations along a small hillslope. These sensors also collect soil temperature and bulk conductance. In addition, some collocated sensors provide pore pressure and Photochemical Reflectance Index (PRI). The GWT depth has been inferred from various type of Onset pressure transducers. The pressure measurements have been corrected for atmospheric pressure variations and sensor position relative to the ground surface to infer GWT depth, as well as with RTK GPS data to infer GWT elevation. The GWT data have been acquired at 5 distinct locations from 2020 to 2024 with the sensors placed at about 4 m depth. In addition, GWT data has been acquired for the 2023-2024 period with sensors located in 1 m deep shallow wells installed near each deeper well. This data is intended to evaluate possibly different dynamic in shallow (perched) and deep aquifer. The datasets are all provided in csv format. Please note that the interpretation of the GWT data needs to be done with consideration of environmental and well characteristics at the site and uncertainty in various variables. For more information on GWT and SM data, please contact the author.

measurementTechnique:
Depth profiles of soil moisture (SM) sensors are present at 5 locations along an about 150 m long transect with 7 meters elevation range. Each location corresponds to one data file containing the data from sensors at multiple depths, starting in 2021. The number at the end of each file name (starting with z6) indicates the location, with 1 (SM1) located on the upper part and 5 (SM5) at the bottom of the hillslope. Also, SM1 to 5 have serial numbers 11599, 11607, 11601, 11602 and 11606, respectively (provided in their file name). In each file, the Port 1, 2, 3, 4 correspond to sensors at depth of 90, 60, 30, 10 cm, respectively. For each Port (1 to 4) the provided values are Soil moisture, Soil Temperature and Soil Conductance. Port 5 provides Matric Potential of a sensor located at 30 cm depth.
In addition, SM1, SM3 and SM5 have a PRI sensor plugged to the logger in port 6 (see the last columns in these files). It measures upwelling radiation at 532 nm and 570 nm, generally used to calculate PRI (https://www.metergroup.com/en/meter-environment/education-guides/ndvi-and-pri-researchers-complete-guide). Two additional loggers measure the downwelling radiation (with diffusers instead of the directional sensors used for upwelling) at SM1 and SM3 locations. The additional loggers for SM1 and SM3 are named with “up” in their file names and have their serial number added, 01502 and 01420, respectively. These PRI sensors are part of an old generation of sensors in the METER product line and should be interpreted carefully (needs some comparison with the Flux/weather tower at the site to ensure the values make sense).
Groundwater table (GWT) depth and elevation are also provided for several locations across the site. Along the intensive transect, WL_top, WL_mid and WL_bot (these three wells are sometimes referred to with a S in front of top, bot and mid for reference to South) are collocated near SM2, SM3 and SM5, respectively. WL_Ntop, WL_Nbot are located on the northern part of the site. Each of the 5 wells has been equipped with a pressure transducer at about 4 m depth and data collection started in 2020 or later. Data have been processed to correct for atmospheric pressure variations and sensor position in order to infer GWT depth and then elevation using RTK GPS data. While GWT rises up to the top meter in the winter, GWT is in several locations deeper than the sensor in the summer and thus data are sparser in the summer. In each file provided, the second column provides the water table elevation, and the third one the water table depth (below ground surface).
Five more wells have been installed in March 2023 for monitoring GWT in the top meter next to the 5 deeper wells to evaluate the possible seasonal presence of shallow perched aquifer. The dataset is also provided here. Please note that the comparison between the shallow well data and the deeper well data is possible in relative term but not in absolute yet. Uncertainty remains on the exact positioning of the shallow well sensors, and will require some manual measurements of GWT depth in all the wells at a future time. The archive will be updated accordingly. At this time, the data are shifted to have similar GWT depth as in deep wells when the GWT depth is very shallow (when we expect similar values in shallow and deep well except if vertical flow is present, or if the lower aquifer is under pressure which would implies higher pressure (and shallow estimated GWT) for the deeper wells, which is not the case here). To obtain similar GWT depth values at time when shallow GWT was present, the SHWL1 to 5 GWT depth (in the provided files) has be shifted down 0.2 m, 0.02 m, 0.15, 0.09, 0.08 for the SHWL_top, SHWL_mid, SHWL_bot, SHWL_Ntop, SHWL_Nbot, respectively. Subtracting these values to the GWT depth provide the original values. The archive will possibly be updated at later time based on new data.
All time are in PST, all coordinates are UTM zone 10N.
Please do not hesitate to contact the author if you have questions.
